To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SARS CoV 1 and SARS CoV-2 infections may accelerate the onset of T2DM by inducing b cell dysfunction and/or apoptosis, and that these effects are mediated through the renin angiotension aldosterone system, oxidative stress, inflammation, and islet fibrosis.

COVID 19 may result in the development of T2DM by inducing b cell dysfunction and/or apoptosis and that the mechanisms involved may include the renin angiotension aldosterone system, oxidative stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and amyloidosis.
COVID 19 may result in T2DM as one of its complications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of SARS CoV 19 and the resulting cytokine storm and the role it has in the development of T2DM and its complications.
the mechanisms of islet and b cells dysfunction, b cell apoptosis, and the role of islet renin-angiotensin system in COVID 19 and T2DM.
the role of COVID 19 in the development of T2DM and the possible mechanisms of b cell dysfunction and injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
COVID 19 is a major cause of T2DM, which may result in a new pandemic.
the COVID 19 virus and the host's response to it may be responsible for a remarkable increase in the incidence of T2DM, a condition that may be difficult to treat and manage.
the COVID 19 pandemic may be a harbinger of an accelerated and widespread development of T2DM in the general population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
COVID 19 may accelerate islet injury, b cell dysfunction, and apoptosis to result in the development of T2DM as a complication.

COVID 19 is associated with a remarkable increase in the risk of T2DM and that this is likely to be due to the direct and indirect effects of SARS CoV 19 on pancreatic islets and the b cells within them.
SARS CoV 19 infection may cause T2DM in those who have not yet developed this condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
COVID 19 may accelerate the development of T2DM in susceptible individuals.
COVID 19 may cause T2DM in a subset of individuals who have pre existing risk factors for diabetes and metabolic syndrome.
COVID 19 is a b cell killer, which may lead to the development of T2DM in the long term, and that the islet renin-angiotensin system may play a central role in this process.
